It is therefore a challenging task to design suitable statistical models and to develop effective reverse engineering algorithms. The signature of noise is pervasive in genetic networks. For instance, in perturbation experiments only a few genes change expression value, while most genes are either noisy or constant. Consequently, a genetic regulatory network is a redundant system, due to the high-dimensionality and the dependence between genes, and also a sparse system through the gene-gene interaction matrix only partially active. In order to explore these two aspects, redundancy and sparsity, independent component analysis (ICA) is proposed as a flexible approximation model targeted to dimensionality reduction and gene feature selection. </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1142/s0219477505002811\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2005, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/icrai68431.2025.11396700\", \"title\": [\"Noise-Robustness Analysis of Hybrid Quantum-Classical CNNs for Small-Sample Road Image Classification\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/icrai68431.2025.11396700\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 19]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-1-4419-6624-7_4\", \"title\": [\"How Does Noise Affect a Quantum State?\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4419-6624-7_4\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 12, 15]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "e5ee46c76d7ab1f00bb33a03849d75614ff29c51b3a3be133a7ababb88c9043d", "verificatio…
